resources.string: Enables Home screen app search, Backspace-as-Back outside text fields, double-tap media controls, and speed keys for your physical keyboard. Does not read or send passwords or screen text.

%1$s exists but cannot be opened: %2$s. The system build with SELinux access is required.
The case is probed when it appears and on request only: every request is a USB write, and writes to a sleeping case cause kernel warnings.
No 0661:0881 device in /sys/bus/usb/devices (absent or not readable).

The case has a battery, but it belongs to a separate power and charging chip. The case controller does not report it: neither the HID descriptor nor the 0x4B protocol carries charge or power state. This section shows the Type-C roles and the phone battery.
The phone is the VBUS source: it powers the case.
The phone is a sink: it takes power from the partner.
No input device with vendor 0661 and product 0881.

Read-only GET 0x00 reads of the case RAM, at most 14 words per request. Addresses come from the 2026-11-01 RAM dump map; only entries with high raw confidence are shown. Meanings marked unverified are not proven.
All table values are zero: this may be an echo reply rather than memory.
f = frequency u16 (0x1140BC), Q = raw u16 (0x11415C, /256 unverified), G = gain s16 (0x1141FC, /256 unverified).
No case transport. Connect the case or enable demo mode.

Both getters answer with a signed int16 in 1/256 dB. By the firmware code, 0x02 is the microphone gain applied in the controller and 0x03 is added to the headphone DAC attenuation. Not checked by ear.

8 bands per bank, banks 0–8. Bank 0 replies were captured on the device; the field meanings (frequency, Q×256, gain×256, filter type, preamp) follow the vendor tool and firmware disassembly and are unverified for sound.
Global audio state read from the controller RAM (GET 0x00). Field meanings come from the firmware disassembly and are not verified by ear.
Writes the DAC filter byte in RAM (reset-safe, lost on unplug; device-unverified). It takes effect on the next sample-rate change, so switch the Android output rate after setting it.
Set the DAC digital filter to \"%1$s\"? This writes case RAM and is lost when the case is unplugged.
Writes are off. Enable them in Settings to edit EQ bands or send 0x0A.
0x0A with the vendor payload 00 00 FF FF; the vendor tool sends it after band writes. Effect on this firmware is unverified.

Unchanged filter fields keep the coefficients read from the case. Otherwise the app computes cookbook biquad coefficients in Q2.30 at the sample rate chosen in Settings; the stored bank 0 coefficients match this formula at 96 kHz.
Send SET 0x09 for bank %1$d band %2$d: %3$d Hz, Q %4$.3f, gain %5$.2f, type %6$d, preamp %7$d? The effect is unverified. The app checks the version first and reads the band back.
Send SET 0x0A 00 00 FF FF? The effect is unverified.

Writes send SET commands to the case RAM (EQ 0x09/0x0A, microphone gain 0x02, the DAC filter byte) whose audible effect is not verified on this firmware. Commands that write the case flash (0x01, 0x04, 0x05) are never sent. Enable?
Press keys on the case. Back closes the tester.

Off by default. When on, the Audio screen can send SET 0x09, 0x0A and 0x02 and the DAC filter RAM byte, each after a confirmation and a version probe. Commands that write the case flash (0x01, 0x04, 0x05) are never sent. Service mode (Service screen) has its own confirmation and only reads.
Replays replies measured on the device (version V0.1, gains 0, bank 0 EQ, flash header) so the app works without the case.
Used only to compute coefficients for edited bands. 96 kHz reproduces the stored bank 0 coefficients exactly.
Snap Case controls the iKKO Snap keyboard case (USB 0661:0881) of the iKKO MindOne. Licensed under the Apache License 2.0.
The case is in BROM service mode (0666:0888): keyboard and sound are off until it returns.
What the Android audio stack sees of the case DAC: rates, channel counts and encodings from AudioDeviceInfo, and whether a bit-perfect mixer is offered.
SET 0x02 changes the microphone gain in the case RAM: the firmware rounds it to 1.5 dB steps, recomputes the capture gain and does not save it to flash. It resets on reconnect.
Range −24…+12 dB as in the vendor tool. After the write the app reads GET 0x02 back and compares it with the rounded value.
Send SET 0x02 with %1$+.1f dB? RAM only, not saved to flash. The app probes the version first and reads the gain back.

Memory, buses and the case log
Developer access is time-limited. Reads cannot harm the case; register writes, I2C and the audio bench can, so use them only when you know the hardware.

Kumi %1$s is custom firmware for this case: settings that survive sleep, a parametric equalizer, key remapping in the case and safe updates. The stock firmware is backed up first and you can go back at any time.
Demo mode: a simulated case runs the real installer, updater and restore code.
The Kumi library is missing from this build.
This build has no release key, so firmware cannot be verified and installing is off. Demo mode shows the whole flow.
No verified firmware in the app yet. Check releases below.
No backup saved on this phone. The case keeps its own backup copy and uses it if you restore.
Returns your case to the original factory firmware at any time.

The case restarts into service mode, the stock firmware is written back and verified, and the case restarts. Keep it attached and tap Shift on the case every 1–2 minutes so it stays awake; this takes about two minutes.

The case enters service mode, its whole flash is backed up to this phone, then Kumi is written and verified step by step. Typing and audio stop for about three minutes. Tap Shift on the case every 1–2 minutes during backup and writing so its 3-minute auto-sleep timer does not pause the transfer. Every step can be resumed after an interruption, and you can return to the stock firmware at any time.
Keep the case attached. The screen stays on automatically until this finishes.
Tap Shift on the case every 1–2 minutes
Service mode cannot pause the case\'s 3-minute auto-sleep timer. Tapping Shift keeps it awake without typing anything. If it sleeps anyway, press any key and tap Resume.
The update is installed and confirmed.

Keeps the case in Kumi low-power sleep (DAC off) instead of disconnecting after 3 minutes while the screen or PC is active. Still sleeps fully when USB suspends; may slightly increase phone standby drain.

10-band studio EQ, saved settings, key layers & full factory backup
Stock firmware forgets sound settings whenever the case sleeps after 3 minutes. Kumi stores everything inside the case and restores it automatically.
4-tier CPU clock scaling (30–360 MHz), 1.4 V external DC-DC, ~99.5% WFI idle sleep, deep DAC and I2S shutdown when silent, and 1 Vrms low-gain mode keep battery drain and heat to a minimum.

10-band parametric EQ with 8 research presets (Harman Target, Studio Neutral, Late Night…), dynamic ISO 226 loudness, spatial sound, peak protection, L/R swap, DC + 1 kHz AC headphone check and volume limit.
In-case key layers, combos & mouse keys
4 keyboard layers, Tap/Hold keys, sticky modifiers, 8 key combos, Caps Word, HID mouse keys and macros run directly inside the case — works on both phone and computer with no background service.
Dual A/B slots roll back automatically if an update ever fails. Your original firmware is backed up twice before anything is written, and you can return to factory firmware anytime.

1. Switch the case into maintenance mode
2. Read & verify a full backup of your original firmware
3. Write & verify Kumi step by step (tap Shift every 1–2 min to keep the case awake; resumable if interrupted)
4. Restart into Kumi — no root required
